To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) monoclonal antibodies are useful for the serotyping of human and simian rotavirus strains and (2) the use of monoclonal antibody-based enzyme immunoassays for serotyping faecal extracts is specific but lacks sufficient sensitivity.

(1) monoclonal antibodies can be used to type rotavirus strains, (2) rotavirus strains can be classified into four serotypes and (3) the serotype-specific monoclaonal antibodies can be used in an EIA to detect rotavirus in faeces.
(1) the panel of monocloal antibodies is specific for human rotavirus serotypes and (2) the EIA using monoclonal antibody is specific for serotyping of rotavirus isolations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a simple and rapid serotyping method using monoclonal antibody EIA which will be useful for the epidemiological surveillance of rotavirus disease.
the development of monoclonal antibody reagents which will allow rapid and accurate serotyping of human rotavirus strains.
the development of monoclonal antibody probes for the serotyping of rotavirus strains and the use of these probes for the study of rotavirus antigenic variation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

these monoclonal antibody reagents are useful for the identification of HRV serotypes 1-4 and SA11 in neutralization tests but are not sufficiently sensitive to be used in the direct identification of HRV in faecal extracts.
the panel of five monoclonal antibodies has been shown to be specific and sensitive for the serotyping of HRV strains in both neutralization and EIA tests.
, in general, the serotyping of rotavirus strains by neutralization tests is more specific than the serotyping of faecal extracts by enzyme immunoassays.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
these monoclonal antibody reagents are valuable for the identification and classification of human rotavirus isolates.

the monoclonal antibody panel can be used to serotype HRV isolates, but that the panel is limited to the four serotypes and SA11 and cannot detect serological differences between strains within a serotype, nor can it detect antigenic differences between serotypes 1a and 1b.

the panel of neutralizing monoclonals can be used to confirm serotype assignments made using polyclonal sera, but the panel of neutralizers is not sensitive enough to be used for direct serotyping in EIA.

these monoclonal antibody reagents can be used for the serotype-specific diagnosis and typing of rotavirus isolants in the clinical laboratory.
